standard_treatment.surgery: Maximal tumor resection, key prognostic factor
standard_treatment.combined_therapy: Stupp regimen: TMZ + RT, increases OS by 2.5 months

treatment_challenges: TMZ resistance rate up to 90%, median OS only 14.6 months
Poor prognosis for recurrent GBM, median OS 3-9 months
Blood-brain barrier limits drug entry into tumor tissue
Tumor heterogeneity and stem cells cause treatment failure
Immune microenvironment suppresses anti-tumor immune response
failed_trials_insights: Single-target inhibitors failed: strong tumor adaptability, pathway redundancy
Immunotherapy monotherapy failed: complex GBM immunosuppressive microenvironment
Insufficient BBB penetration: most drugs cannot reach effective concentrations
Narrow therapeutic window: normal brain tissue damage limits dosage
successful_patterns: Multi-target synergy: simultaneous inhibition of multiple key pathways
BBB optimization: lipophilicity optimization, active transport mechanisms
Immunotherapy combinations: targeted therapy + immune checkpoint inhibition
Stem cell targeting: elimination of tumor-initiating cells

classical.characteristics: EGFR amplification, wild-type p53, high NES expression
classical.treatment_response: Sensitive to EGFR inhibitors, but prone to resistance

mesenchymal.characteristics: NF1 loss, MET amplification, high inflammation-related gene expression
mesenchymal.treatment_response: Sensitive to anti-inflammatory therapy, relatively poor prognosis

proneural.treatment_response: Sensitive to differentiation induction, relatively better prognosis

neural.characteristics: High neural marker expression, strong heterogeneity

prognostic.MGMT_methylation: Chemotherapy sensitivity marker, better prognosis with methylation
